newsitem.title: USA: S&P raises Boeing, McDonnell Douglas ratings.
newsitem.headline: S&P raises Boeing, McDonnell Douglas ratings.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said Thursday it has raised its ratings on Boeing Co, McDonnell Douglas Corp and McDonnell Douglas Finance Corp.
All ratings have been removed from CreditWatch where they were placed December 16, 1996, the rating agency noted.

The upgrade on Boeing recognizes the strengthening of its business and financial profiles following the merger with McDonnell Douglas Corp in a stock transaction valued at about $16 billion, S&P said, explaining the combination will substantially enhance Boeing's position as the world's largest aerospace firm.

The addition of McDonnell Douglas, a leading military contractor and the largest producer of military aircraft, will significantly improve Boeing's competitive posture in the defense sector. This complements Boeing's already prominent position in the commercial aircraft manufacturing industry.
S&P said significant merger synergies are anticipated, although they will probably take years to realize and restructuring charges are likely.
The addition of McDonnell Douglas' profitability and cash flows of its military businesses, coupled with moderate debt levels, enhances Boeing's already strong financial profile.
That profile is characterized by impressive cash flow generation, relatively low debt levels, and sizable cash balances exceeding debt.
S&P said McDonnell Douglas ratings are raised to the level of Being's credit quality, reflecting the importance of McDonnell Douglas' operations to Boeing.

The upgrade on McDonnell Douglas Finance reflects the benefits of the merger, including the 100 percent indirect ownership by Boeing. But the finance unit's ratings are not equalized with Boeing's because there is some uncertainty about the fit of financial services in Boeing's long-term mix.

S&P said the outlook for Boeing and McDonnell Douglas is stable, explaining the expected continuation of the current upturn in commercial aerospace, stabilization of the defense procurement budgets, a very strong financial profile, and actions to improve efficiencies should maintain credit quality, despite the highly competitive, cyclical and capital- intensive nature of the commercial aircraft market and very competitive conditions in the defense sector.
The rating agency said McDonnell Douglas Finance's ooutlook is developing, adding that ratings could be raised if the unit is retained as a continuing operation of Boeing.
Ratings could be lowered if the unit is divested to a
weaker entity. RATINGS RAISED AND REMOVED FROM CREDITWATCH
